organization: Charles B. Wang Community Health Center
program: Multilingual community primary, dental and mental health care

acceptance.evidence: givebetter-nyc-sixth-seventh-independent-acceptance.json: primary-source checks, independent reconstruction of every scenario, and explicit uncertainty review; accepted as conditional alpha modeling, not measured causal impact.

what: CBWCHC delivers multilingual primary, dental and mental-health care in Manhattan and Queens.
It reported over 70,000 patients in 2025, but patient counts and quality awards do not identify additional health caused by gifts.
A weak-confidence whole-recipient model implies about $24.3 million per 10 NYC-MSA QALYs.
strengths: Direct clinical services provide a tangible health mechanism.
Language access and reduced fees address barriers even among insured patients.
Current original financial and patient reporting supports an explicit whole-recipient model.
reservations: No controlled incremental utility estimate is available for this recipient.
Most revenue comes from existing patient services and other funding, making gift additionality uncertain.
Patient residence and effective care relative to alternative providers are not reported at the required MSA granularity.

sections.what: The center offers medical, dental, mental-health, social-work and support services at clinical sites in Manhattan and Queens. Its multilingual staffing can improve access and continuity. Services span prevention and chronic disease management; a visit is not equivalent to an additional healthy year. [Services and history](https://www.cbwchc.org/about-us) [Locations](https://www.cbwchc.org/locations)
sections.monitoring: Request patient-level residence, treatment completion, baseline severity and quality-of-life change, with alternative-provider comparison and durable follow-up. HRSA quality awards and screening performance demonstrate delivery quality, not donor causation. Oregon insurance randomization supplies a cautionary analogy: access can improve mental health while short-term measured physical effects remain undetected. It does not validate our clinic utility coefficient. [Original randomized evidence](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMsa1212321)
sections.qualitative: Language-concordant care may prevent misunderstandings and help people navigate specialist referrals. The counterfactual includes other community centers, hospitals and insured physician care; an uninsured-only screen would also miss real language barriers. Conversely, treating every existing patient as dependent on a donation greatly overstates marginal impact. [Provider context](https://www.cbwchc.org/about-us)
sections.cost: The central model retains $97,126,149 of annual recipient expense and 70,000 patients, rounded down from the reported lower threshold. It assumes 20% receive effective care beyond alternatives, 0.02 utility gain for 0.5 years, 30% marginal gift additionality and 95% MSA residence: 70,000 × 0.2 × 0.02 × 0.5 × 0.3 × 0.95 =39.9 MSA QALYs. This is $24,342,393 per 10 QALYs. These clinical and allocation coefficients are transparent judgments, not observed causal effects. No mortality credit or future-year persistence is added. External hospital, medication and household costs are excluded. An illustrative $1,000 of whole-portfolio cost corresponds to 0.721 historical patient equivalents before clinical, geographic and financial adjustments; this is not a promised extra patient or measured marginal unit cost.
sections.funding:
The 2025 annual report's financial page reports $82,219,650 program expenses plus $14,906,499 general/administrative expense, totaling $97,126,149. Revenue is $89,787,848, of which $61,388,351 is patient services; the reported decrease in net assets is $7,338,301. Audit status, precise period dates and consolidation detail are not provided on that page, so no audited three-year mean is claimed. [Original report, printed page 11](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65525600ad11f5d8bc8c3450/6a21d66b1ec4b680b9058e9a_2025%20CBWCHC%20Annual%20Report_ForWeb.pdf)

Giving is directed to the operating health center; the official page identifies programs exceeding conventional reimbursement. A budget deficit does not prove a 30% gift elasticity; unrestricted gifts may replace funds or maintain existing care. Our model follows the recipient-wide mix without claiming a restricted offer. [Official donation page](https://www.cbwchc.org/give)

model.costScope: Full expense reported in2025 recipient annual report, not sponsor/related-foundation revenue or charity-care discount valuation. Hospital/referral/pharmaceutical costs outside reported expense excluded.
model.geographicAttribution: g=.95 judgment: clinical sites in Manhattan and Queens, but residences not supplied. Central allows5% outside the 22-county MSA; g=.8 to1 sensitivity. Site address alone does not establish resident share.
model.formula: Q_all=N*a*u*t*b; Q_MSA=Q_all*g; cost=C*f; price10=10*cost/Q_MSA. Mortality=0; health ends at t.
model.counterfactual: Existing public/private insurance, federal grants, alternative community providers and other donors continue. a=.2 isolates care beyond alternatives; b=.3 separately accounts for donation-financing substitution.
model.attribution: Ordinary unrestricted gifts assumed to support recipient-wide mix at average resource cost, scaled by .3 marginal capacity factor. No gift is automatically credited with all existing clinical visits.
model.uncertainty: Weak-confidence utility and additionality model; no recipient-specific QALY study, measured gift elasticity, or patient residence distribution. Scenario endpoints are judgments, not confidence limits.
model.nativeOutcomes: Distinct annual patients receiving additional effective clinical care, mapped to finite utility gain; visits, insurance status and quality awards do not independently add health.

inputs.name: C
inputs.rationale: All reported program and general/administrative expenses; no sponsor denominator.

inputs.name: f
inputs.rationale: Constant2025 expense before sensitivity; no scale economies assumed.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: 20%of observed patient volume represents effective care beyond alternatives; unmeasured.

inputs.name: u
inputs.rationale: Mean.02 improvement among additional effective-care recipients; explicit judgment, not Oregon coefficient.

inputs.name: t
inputs.rationale: Half-year average health improvement; no gain after this window.

inputs.name: b
inputs.rationale: 30% after alternative funding and capacity constraints; unmeasured.

inputs.name: g
inputs.rationale: 95% judged from five clinical sites; no patient residence dataset.

sensitivity: At g=.8 central price rises to approximately$28.9m/10; at g=1 it is approximately$23.1m/10.
If b=.1 instead of.3, price triples. If benefit lasts .25 years instead of.5, price doubles.
A net39.9-QALY harm/displacement term offsets central geographic gain; unmeasured harms are not established zero.
